config.title: Build end to end capstone React plus TS enterprise dashboard

intro.title: Build end to end capstone React plus TS enterprise dashboard
intro.body: In this capstone project, you will build a complete enterprise dashboard application from scratch using React and TypeScript. You will learn how to structure a real-world project by creating reusable components, managing application state, and fetching data from an API. The core programming concepts you will practice include defining strict TypeScript interfaces for your data, using React hooks for state and side effects, and composing components to build a complex UI. By the end, you will have a functional dashboard that displays key metrics and charts, solidifying your understanding of how React and TypeScript work together in a professional front-end application.
intro.usecase: This lesson builds a comprehensive enterprise dashboard, a core UI pattern used in real-world business applications like Salesforce, Google Analytics, and internal admin panels. Developers implement these dashboards to display key metrics, interactive charts, and data tables for monitoring performance, sales, or system health. Mastering this pattern equips you to create data-rich, maintainable interfaces that are central to modern SaaS products and internal tools, where TypeScript ensures data integrity and React enables dynamic, component-based updates.

objectives: Construct a TypeScript interface to define the shape of dashboard data
Initialize and manage component state with typed React hooks
Implement reusable functional components with typed props
Configure event handlers to manipulate dashboard state
Integrate multiple components to build a complete dashboard layout
Render dynamic content by mapping over typed data arrays
Apply TypeScript generics to create flexible utility functions

steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.instruction: Import React and useState from 'react' to enable component creation and state management.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in the necessary modules. The syntax is: import { React, useState } from 'react';
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing modules for a component
import { React, useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: The necessary React modules are imported, setting up the foundation for the dashboard component.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but ensure both React and useState are imported from 'react'. Check your import statement.
steps.feedbackWrong: The import statement is missing or incorrect. Please import React and useState from 'react' to proceed.

steps.title: Create the main Dashboard component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named Dashboard that returns a div element.
steps.hint: Define the component using either a function declaration or arrow function syntax. Remember to include the return statement with the div.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Create the Dashboard component here
steps.expectedOutcome: The Dashboard component is defined and returns a div element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure the Dashboard component returns a div element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Dashboard component isn't defined correctly. Check that you've created a functional component named Dashboard that returns a div.

steps.title: Define the DashboardData interface
steps.instruction: Create a TypeScript interface named DashboardData with three properties: totalUsers (number), revenue (number), and activeProjects (number). Place it above the Dashboard component.
steps.hint: Use the 'interface' keyword followed by the interface name and property definitions with type annotations.
steps.expectedOutcome: A DashboardData interface is defined with the correct properties and types.
successCriteria: DashboardData interface exists with totalUsers: number, revenue: number, and activeProjects: number properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure all three properties (totalUsers, revenue, activeProjects) are defined with the 'number' type.
steps.feedbackWrong: The interface definition is missing or incorrect. Remember to use the 'interface' keyword and define all three properties with 'number' type.

steps.title: Initialize dashboard state with useState
steps.instruction: Inside your Dashboard component, use the useState hook to create a state variable named dashboardData of type DashboardData. Initialize it with default values: totalUsers: 0, activeSessions: 0, revenue: 0, and topProduct: 'None'.
steps.hint: Call useState<DashboardData>() with the initial object containing the four properties from your interface.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: typed state initialization
const [user, setUser] = useState<User>({ name: '', age: 0 });
steps.expectedOutcome: The dashboardData state variable is properly typed and initialized with default values.
successCriteria: dashboardData state is declared with useState<DashboardData> and initialized with an object containing all four properties from the interface.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using the DashboardData type with useState and providing all four properties (totalUsers, activeSessions, revenue, topProduct) with default values.
steps.feedbackWrong: The state initialization is missing or incorrect. Remember to use useState<DashboardData> with an initial object containing all properties from the DashboardData interface.

steps.title: Create a function to update dashboard metrics
steps.instruction: Inside the Dashboard component, create a function named updateMetrics that takes a parameter of type Partial<DashboardData> and updates the dashboardData state using the setDashboardData function.
steps.hint: Use the setDashboardData function from useState to update the state. The function should accept an object with partial dashboard data and merge it with the current state.
steps.expectedOutcome: A typed updateMetrics function is added to the Dashboard component that can handle partial updates to the dashboard state.
successCriteria: The updateMetrics function is defined with correct TypeScript typing and properly updates the dashboardData state.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure the function accepts Partial<DashboardData> and properly updates the state using setDashboardData.
steps.feedbackWrong: The updateMetrics function is missing or has incorrect implementation. It should accept Partial<DashboardData> and update the state.

steps.title: Add a container div with dashboard class
steps.instruction: In the Dashboard component's return statement, replace the current return value with a div element that has className='dashboard'.
steps.hint: The return statement should now output a div with the specified class name instead of null.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Dashboard component now returns a div element with the class 'dashboard' as its root container.
successCriteria: The return statement contains a div element
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've replaced 'null' with a div element that has className='dashboard'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The return statement should output a div element with className='dashboard' instead of null.

steps.title: Add a header element with dashboard title
steps.instruction: Inside the Dashboard component's return statement, add an h1 element with the text 'Enterprise Dashboard'.
steps.hint:
The h1 element should be placed inside the container div you created earlier. Use JSX syntax:

Enterprise Dashboard
steps.expectedOutcome: The dashboard container now contains a header with the title 'Enterprise Dashboard'.
successCriteria: An h1 element is added inside the container div
The h1 element contains the text 'Enterprise Dashboard'
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added an element, but make sure it's an h1 with exactly the text 'Enterprise Dashboard' inside the container div.
steps.feedbackWrong:
The header element wasn't added correctly. Remember to add

Enterprise Dashboard

inside the container div in your return statement.

steps.title: Display total users metric card
steps.instruction: Inside the metrics container div, add a new div element with className='metric-card' that displays the total users value from dashboardData with a descriptive label.
steps.hint: Use JSX to create a div with the specified class, then display dashboardData.totalUsers inside it along with a label like 'Total Users'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: rendering a data value in a styled card

Total Users

{dashboardData.totalUsers}
steps.expectedOutcome: The metrics container now contains a styled card displaying the total users value from the dashboard state.
successCriteria: A div with className='metric-card' is added inside the metrics-container
The div displays dashboardData.totalUsers with a descriptive label
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a metric card, but make sure it displays dashboardData.totalUsers with a clear label.
steps.feedbackWrong: The metric card for total users wasn't properly implemented. Check that you're using the correct className and accessing dashboardData.totalUsers.

steps.title: Display revenue metric card
steps.instruction: Inside the metrics container, add a second metric card that displays the revenue value from dashboardData with proper formatting (e.g., '$' prefix).
steps.hint: Add another div with a class like 'metric-card' and display dashboardData.revenue inside it. You can format it as currency using template literals or toLocaleString.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: displaying a formatted value

Revenue

${dashboardData.revenue.toLocaleString()}
steps.expectedOutcome: A second metric card appears in the dashboard showing the revenue value with currency formatting.
successCriteria: A div with a class like 'metric-card' is added inside the metrics container, displaying dashboardData.revenue with a '$' prefix or proper formatting.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a revenue metric card, but it may be missing proper formatting (like a '$' prefix) or the correct class name. Check the formatting and ensure it's inside the metrics container.
steps.feedbackWrong: The revenue metric card is not present or incorrectly placed. Make sure to add a div inside the metrics container that displays dashboardData.revenue with currency formatting.

steps.title: Display active projects metric card
steps.instruction: Add a third metric card inside the metrics-container div to display the activeSessions value from dashboardData.
steps.hint: Create a new div with class 'metric-card' containing a heading for 'Active Sessions' and a paragraph showing dashboardData.activeSessions.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a metric card

Active Sessions

{dashboardData.activeSessions}
steps.expectedOutcome: The metrics container will have three metric cards showing total users, revenue, and active sessions values.
successCriteria: A third metric card element with class 'metric-card' is added inside the metrics-container, displaying the activeSessions value from dashboardData.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a metric card, but make sure it displays the activeSessions value from dashboardData and has the correct structure.
steps.feedbackWrong: The active sessions metric card is missing or incorrect. Add a div with class 'metric-card' containing a heading and paragraph showing dashboardData.activeSessions.

steps.title: Add refresh button and wire onClick handler
steps.instruction: Add a button element with the text 'Refresh Data' inside the metrics container, and wire its onClick handler to call the updateMetrics function with new values.
steps.hint: Place the button after the metric cards. Use onClick={handleRefresh} and define a handleRefresh function that calls updateMetrics with updated data.
steps.expectedOutcome: A 'Refresh Data' button appears below the metric cards. Clicking it updates all dashboard metrics with realistic sample data.
successCriteria: Button with text 'Refresh Data' is present in metrics container
handleRefresh function calls updateMetrics with new values
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've added the button element with the correct text and wired its onClick to the handleRefresh function that calls updateMetrics.
steps.feedbackWrong: The refresh button isn't working correctly. Check that you've added the button element with 'Refresh Data' text and properly connected it to the updateMetrics function through the onClick handler.
